<description>
This fixes an antithesis bug reported in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35845 and similar bug reported in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/33387 where if asynchronous IPC mining calls are made when the node is shutting down it's possible for `assert(m_node.chainman)` to trigger. This happens because the `Ipc::disconnectIncoming` method does not wait for asynchronous calls to complete after it disconnects IPC clients, so they may continue to run as the node is shutting down.

This PR changes `disconnectIncoming` to wait for asynchronous calls to complete to avoid this issue. It's a draft because it depends on libmultiprocess changes, but should otherwise be ready to review.

**This is based on bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#361 and bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#335,** included through a `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree update that also contains bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#377, which this PR does not need.

The non-base commits are:

- [`8a948e2bdd4` doc: Improve disconnect callback comments](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/8a948e2bdd4d2f48cd5a5c9ffd9e0660b0769c15)
- [`59f703760b2` doc: Improve Waiter/EventLoop lock order documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/59f703760b292fdf5d35c36ef55298b58df11dc7)
- [`98533b0201e` proxy-io: fix listener stuck at capacity after a local disconnect](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/98533b0201e5eeb6b2c9c07c3e48525266fd9b3d)
- [`0b1730bad11` proxy-io: fix race deleting a disconnected Connection twice](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/0b1730bad1191e2a230962aaad2feeb83c003c4f)
- [`789775cb46c` proxy: Fix thread map teardown race causing use-after-free on disconnect](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/789775cb46cb95c1e697ff23d6f8b63be59caf82)
- [`580d9644a71` proxy-io: add Connection::disconnect() separating teardown from destruction](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/580d9644a712dc41588ed0c2fa35b2b6bda6eec3)
- [`bb588048d12` proxy-io: add Connection::waitDrained() to wait for in-flight server calls](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/bb588048d12dd3d331d01b736fcfd9092cdf6222)
- [`0ad96a7fab3` test: cover draining in-flight server call after disconnect](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/0ad96a7fab3293d663c3c2b0235f4741bbb9f6f7)
- [`d9ffa655294` ipc: use ServeStream/ConnectStream in Bitcoin Core IPC code](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/d9ffa65529468a88a2ad01852e2d643768314af8)
- [`dc293af2f43` ipc: drain in-flight server calls before shutdown frees node state](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/dc293af2f4319f6cee434ade12083e441aafaeea)
- [`01a01e35d97` lint: Skip subtree check for src/ipc/libmultiprocess](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932/commits/01a01e35d9732268e09cfa524c55128389cccfd5)

### Status (2026-11-13)

This is a draft with no reviews yet. It waits on bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#361 and bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#335, both open, and on a subtree update that includes them. Neither has had new reviews since 2026-11-04; bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#335 still has open review comments from before.

- **Remaining work:**
  - Check whether the node may hang at exit when an IPC client is connected at shutdown, since the disconnected connections no longer appear to be destroyed (suspected from the code, not yet reproduced).
  - Add a test that stops the node with a call in progress, and update the code comment and commit message, which describe an earlier version of the change (the comment still says the connections are destroyed and names `mp::Connection::waitDrained`).
</description>

8a948e2bdd doc: Improve disconnect callback comments

This is a documentation-only change meant to make upcoming commits easier to
understand.

This change was written with Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context).

59f703760b doc: Improve Waiter/EventLoop lock order documentation

Correct the ThreadContext "Synchronization note", which said
Waiter::m_mutex must not be locked before EventLoop::m_mutex. That is
the reverse of the documented and actual lock order (Waiter::m_mutex
first, as ~ProxyServer<Thread> does). The constraint it was reaching for
is the EventLoop blocking rule now documented on Waiter::m_mutex.

This change was written with Claude Fable 5.1.

98533b0201 proxy-io: fix listener stuck at capacity after a local disconnect

Currently, a ListenConnections listener that reaches its max-connection limit
stops accepting new connections permanently if one of its connections is closed
locally instead of by a remote disconnect. Closing a connection locally (e.g.
erasing it from m_incoming_connections) leaves the listener's active-connection
count stuck at the limit, so it never resumes accepting.

This happens because the count is decremented by a callback which only fires on
a remote disconnects, not local disconnects. Fix by moving the decrement to
callback which fires on both local and remote disconnects.

Add a regression test that closes a connection locally and checks the listener
resumes accepting; it fails before this change (the listener never accepts the
waiting client) and passes after.

Co-Authored-By: Enoch Azariah <enirox001@gmail.com>
This change was written with Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context).

0b1730bad1 proxy-io: fix race deleting a disconnected Connection twice

Fix a use-after-free, possible since the destroy_connection option was added
in 2019 (c685fa9): a Connection's disconnect handler could run after the
Connection had already been destroyed, deleting it a second time and
crashing. Reported by enirox001 in
https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/335#discussion_r3821831654

Give each Connection a shared_ptr "alive" token that disconnect handlers hold
a weak_ptr to and check before running, so a handler is skipped once its
Connection is gone. Having this check also enables the simplifications
described below.

Previously each Connection kept its disconnect handlers in its own
kj::TaskSet, and when the network disconnected it moved a handler onto the
shared event loop TaskSet with kj::evalLater. Destroying the Connection
destroyed that per-connection TaskSet, canceling a still-pending handler --
but a handler already moved onto the shared TaskSet was no longer canceled
and could run after the Connection was gone. (The evalLater step existed only
to avoid a "promise callback destroyed itself" error when a handler deletes
its own Connection, which the per-connection TaskSet made possible.)

With the token doing the cancellation, neither the per-connection TaskSet nor
the evalLater step is needed, and both are removed.

Co-Authored-By: Enoch Azariah <enirox001@gmail.com>
This change was written with Claude Fable 5.

789775cb46 proxy: Fix thread map teardown race causing use-after-free on disconnect

Fix a race between a thread exiting after making IPC calls and its
connection being destroyed on the event loop thread, which could destroy
the same ProxyClient<Thread> object twice. ~ThreadContext destroyed the
thread-local request_threads/callback_threads maps with no locking while
the SetThread cleanup callback run by ~Connection erased entries from the
same maps. When both ran at once, each side destroyed the entry's
ProxyClient<Thread>, and ~Connection then ran the ProxyClientBase
disconnect callback on the freed map node (heap-use-after-free, then a
glibc "double free or corruption" abort).

Fix by making map entry removal decide which side destroys an entry:
~ThreadContext and the SetThread callback each remove entries under
Waiter::m_mutex before destroying them, and a side that finds an entry
already gone leaves it to the other. See the code comments for why the
entries are destroyed with the mutex released.

Add a regression test, "Thread exiting while its connection is
destroyed", which uses a new testing_hook_thread_client_destroy hook to
interleave the two sides deterministically and fails on every run
without the fix.

The race is long-standing and reachable on master via connections
created by ConnectStream, whose onDisconnect handler deletes the client
Connection on the event loop thread when the peer disconnects.

This change was written with Claude Fable 5.1.

580d9644a7 proxy-io: add Connection::disconnect() separating teardown from destruction

Split connection teardown out of ~Connection into an idempotent disconnect()
method, with the destructor delegating to it. For existing callers, this is a
behavior-neutral refactor: the same steps run in the same order on destruction.

Having a separate disconnect() method allows severing a connection while
keeping the Connection object alive, which the next commits use to let
shutdown code wait for in-flight server call bodies to finish after a
disconnect (bitcoin/bitcoin#35845). Two details are new in the disconnect()
method which were not present in the destructor method:

- disconnect() expires the m_alive token explicitly, where previously it was
  expired implicitly by member destruction. This keeps onRemoteDisconnect able
  to distinguish a local disconnect from a remote one when a connection is
  severed without destroying the object (see the disconnect() code comment).

- disconnect() explicitly releases m_thread_pool and m_thread_map so worker
  thread teardown happens at disconnect time whether or not the object is
  destroyed right away. Previously this happened implicitly during member
  destruction.

This change was written with Claude Fable 5.

bb588048d1 proxy-io: add Connection::waitDrained() to wait for in-flight server calls

Add a per-connection ServerObjectTracker counting live ProxyServer objects,
incremented in the ProxyServerBase constructor and decremented in its
destructor, with Connection::waitDrained() blocking until the count reaches
zero and Connection::pendingServerObjects() exposing it for logging.

Disconnecting a connection cancels the KJ promise of an in-flight call, but a
C++ server method body already dispatched to a worker thread runs to
completion. Counting live server objects turns Cap'n Proto's object lifetime
rules into a usable quiescence signal: a ProxyServer object is not destroyed
until its outstanding calls finish (the target capability is kept alive for
the duration of a call and pinned by post()/PassField via thisCap()), so
after disconnect() the count drains to zero exactly when no server call body
is still executing. Waiting for that lets shutdown code avoid freeing
application state that a still-running call body dereferences
(bitcoin/bitcoin#35845).

The tracker is held via shared_ptr by the Connection and by every
ProxyServer object because objects kept alive by in-flight calls can outlive
the Connection on some teardown paths (see ~ProxyServerBase), and their
destructors must decrement state that is still valid. It must be declared
before m_rpc_system, whose construction creates the bootstrap server object
that registers itself with the tracker.

This change was written with Claude Fable 5.

0ad96a7fab test: cover draining in-flight server call after disconnect

Add a deterministic mptest regression test for bitcoin/bitcoin#35845: hold a
server method body in flight on a worker thread, call
Connection::disconnect(), and assert that Connection::waitDrained() blocks
until the body finishes and its server object is destroyed. Also covers
destroying an already-disconnected connection (~Connection noticing
disconnect() has run).

This change was written with Claude Fable 5.
Co-Authored-By: Enoch Azariah <enirox001@gmail.com>

d9ffa65529 ipc: use ServeStream/ConnectStream in Bitcoin Core IPC code

Replace manual Connection construction in protocol.cpp, ipc_tests.cpp,
and fuzz/ipc.cpp with the ServeStream/ConnectStream helpers added in
preceding commits. None of these call sites need anything the helpers
don't already provide: destroy_connection defaults to true. protocol.cpp
sets m_parent_connection from the connection ServeStream returns, and the
test and fuzz code ignore the return value.

This change was written with Claude Sonnet 5.

dc293af2f4 ipc: drain in-flight server calls before shutdown frees node state

Fix bitcoin/bitcoin#35845, an assertion failure in MinerImpl::chainman()
during shutdown of an IPC-mining node.

Shutdown() calls disconnectIncoming() before node.chainman.reset().
Disconnecting cancels the KJ promise of an in-flight IPC server call, but a
C++ server method body already dispatched to a libmultiprocess worker thread
is not interrupted and runs to completion. A still-running body (an in-flight
Mining.checkBlock) could then dereference m_node.chainman after
chainman.reset() nulled it, aborting on Assert(m_node.chainman).

Make disconnectIncoming() disconnect the non-parent incoming connections,
wait off the event loop thread for their in-flight server call bodies to
finish (Connection::waitDrained), and only then destroy them and return, so
Shutdown() frees node state only once no server code is running. Log when
the wait actually blocks so a shutdown hang here is diagnosable.

No wait is needed for calls parked in waitTipChanged()/waitNext():
Interrupt() runs before Shutdown() and notifies m_tip_block_cv after setting
the shutdown signal, so those return before disconnectIncoming() runs.

Intentional limitations, to keep the fix narrow: m_impl destructors
scheduled on the async cleanup thread are not waited for, the kept-open
parent connection is not drained, and new incoming connections can still be
accepted during shutdown (preventing that needs a listener API, proposed in
bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#269).

This change was written with Claude Fable 5.

01a01e35d9 lint: Skip subtree check for src/ipc/libmultiprocess

WARNING: DO NOT MERGE — this draft PR modifies the libmultiprocess
subtree directly (intentionally, for testing purposes) which causes
the subtree link check to fail. Disabling the check here to avoid
masking unrelated lint failures while the PR is open for testing.

Restore the omitted entry before any merge attempt.

Note: removing src/ipc/libmultiprocess from get_subtrees() also removes
it from get_pathspecs_default_excludes(), so all other lint checks
(trailing newline, whitespace, etc.) now run on files in that directory
as well. This is why src/ipc/libmultiprocess/include/mp/type-unordered-set.h
needs a trailing newline added here even though it is not otherwise
modified by this PR: it has always been missing the newline, but was
previously hidden from the lint check by the subtree exclusion.

This change was written with Claude Sonnet 4.6.

+## [v14.0](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/commits/v14.0)
+- Adds support for nonunix platforms, making API changes that are not backwards compatible ([#274](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/274)). Follow-ups add a `CurrentThread()` accessor matching compatibility code in [bitcoin/bitcoin#35084](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35084) ([#323](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/323)) and remove code for Cap'n Proto versions before 0.9 ([#331](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/331)).
+- Fixes a data race between IPC calls running on worker threads and disconnects, found by Antithesis ([#349](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/349)).
+- Fixes a use-after-free when a socket disconnects before `ConnectStream` connects, and leaks and hangs when a client `construct()` call throws ([#298](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/298)).
+- Fixes a race where file descriptors from `SpawnProcess` could leak into processes forked at the same time by other threads, by clearing `FD_CLOEXEC` in the child after forking ([#311](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/311)).
+- Makes `SpawnProcess` report `exec` failures back to the parent and throw, reaping the child ([#312](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/312)).
+- Adds support for `std::chrono::time_point` fields ([#303](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/303)) and for serializing lists of interface objects that need to be moved from ([#304](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/304)), both needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#10102](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/10102).
+- Accepts container fields and parameters with any comparator, hash, and allocator types, like Bitcoin Core's `GCSFilter::ElementSet`, needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#29409](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409) ([#379](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/379)).
+- Finds the `capnp` tool in vcpkg and Windows builds, needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#32387](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32387) ([#317](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/317)).
+- Adds a `destroy_connection` option to `ServeStream` and `ConnectStream`, lets `ServeStream` take ownership of the init object and return the new server and its connection, and adds an `EventLoop::incomingConnections()` accessor, simplifying test setup in both repositories and needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#35932](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932) ([#365](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/365)).
+- Replaces `EventLoop::post()` with `sync()` taking a `kj::FunctionParam`, avoiding a heap allocation per call ([#347](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/347)).
+- Names threads spawned by the event loop so they can be told apart in tools and logs ([#324](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/324)).
+- Fixes warnings that Bitcoin Core enables or plans to enable: adds `[[noreturn]]` attributes for `-Wmissing-noreturn` ([#339](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/339), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#35911](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35911)), and fixes `-Wunused` ([#362](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/362), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#36167](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36167)), `-Wunused-const-variable` and `-Wundef` ([#370](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/370)), and `-Wmissing-prototypes` ([#386](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/386), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#36743](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36743)) warnings.
+- Fails at compile time with a suggested workaround when Cap'n Proto misdetects exception support (`KJ_NO_EXCEPTIONS`), as happens on NetBSD ([#364](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/364)).
+- Build improvements: fixes stale generated code when the `mpgen` binary changes ([#316](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/316)), fixes `mpgen` link order for static Cap'n Proto builds ([#367](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/367)), links `mpgen` against `kj-async` instead of `capnp-rpc` ([#327](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/327)), shows Cap'n Proto `find_package` diagnostics ([#325](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/325)), installs `type-unordered-set.h` and `version.h` ([#350](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/350)), and shows include-what-you-use errors instead of failing silently ([#371](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/371)).
+- Test, CI, documentation, and minor code improvements: fix for a startup race in the example program ([#315](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/315)), new test for immediate client disconnects in `ListenConnections` ([#310](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/310)), `ReadList` return value check ([#338](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/338)), connect test race fix ([#343](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/343)) and cleanups ([#344](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/344)), `std::ranges::copy` follow-ups ([#307](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/307)), trailing whitespace removal ([#345](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/345)), Cap'n Proto version documentation fix ([#357](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/357)), clang-tidy updates ([#358](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/358), [#360](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/360), [#380](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/380), [#389](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/389)), new CI job testing newer cmake and Cap'n Proto versions ([#212](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/212), [#359](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/359)), CI coverage for the minimum supported g++ ([#330](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/330), [#366](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/366)), new CI warnings ([#332](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/332), [#341](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/341)), CI parallelism ([#334](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/334), [#356](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/356)), CI diagnostics ([#351](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/351), [#352](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/352)), Nix and LLVM updates ([#296](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/296), [#363](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/363)), NetBSD and OpenBSD CI fixes ([#321](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/321), [#340](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/340), [#381](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/381)), building Cap'n Proto with GCC in the 32-bit CI job to avoid an ABI mismatch ([#383](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/383)), and GitHub Actions updates ([#387](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/387)).
+- Used in Bitcoin Core 33.x and newer releases with [#36747](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36747).
